A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of DELIFT. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ICL and QLoRA experiments across three fine-tuning scenarios in Tables 1–6, plus subset-size experiments and judge-score distributions in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B and opt-125m experiments, including GSM-8k evaluation and full fine-tuning comparisons.

M1.justification: Both retain teacher-forced pairwise utilities, FL/FLMI/FLCG objectives and the same greedy Algorithm 1. However, v3 newly suggests clipping utilities to nonnegative similarities, and its practical distance equation omits v1's explicit normalization factor although the prose and Appendix H still specify length-normalized L2. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are documentation changes or actual computation changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds MixInstruct-to-GSM-8k evaluation for multistep mathematical word problems (Table 6). The previous instruction-tuning, question-answering, MT-Bench and proprietary query-rewriting coverage remains. This is a focused extension within task-specific fine-tuning.

E2.justification: DEFT-UCS is newly evaluated in v3 Tables 3, 6 and 9, and Table 6 adds a DELIFT variant using FL instead of FLMI. Comparator membership in the six retained benchmark comparisons is unchanged. Although the continual-tuning prose mentions DEFT-UCS, Tables 7–8 contain no DEFT-UCS results.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation settings through base Llama-3.2-3B and Mistral-7B models and an opt-125m comparison of QLoRA with full fine-tuning. Section 4.5.3 also changes the reported subset-size range from 5–100% to 5–50% in 10% increments, but Appendix B and Figure 2 retain the earlier settings; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct tests of objective choice through FL versus FLMI on GSM-8k (Table 6) and adaptation procedure through QLoRA versus full fine-tuning on opt-125m (Table 9). These substantially extend the questions examined beyond the retained utility-versus-embedding comparisons, subset-size analysis and judge-score distributions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The existing LAJ score-distribution histograms are retained unchanged as Tables 11–12 in v3; they describe response-score variation, not newly introduced uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Tables 1–6 are retained in v3 Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 3, 6 and 9. For example, Mistral/GSM-8k QLoRA LAJ scores are 2.71 for DELIFT, 2.60 for LESS and 2.85 for Full Data. These are newly reported settings, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorems 1–2 and an Appendix A proof that KL-based utility equals conditional pointwise mutual information, including a tokenwise chain-rule decomposition. v1 contains no corresponding derivation. This substantially expands the formal treatment, although the result is conditional on KL divergence and does not prove equivalence for the implemented Euclidean utility. Appendix H also adds an unexplained corr_AB expression.

C1.justification: v3 promotes grounding in conditional pointwise mutual information to a primary contribution, substantially redefining the claimed theoretical basis of the work. v1's separate contribution claiming at least 70% computational-time reduction against gradient methods disappears. The unified three-stage framework and headline claims of 70% data reduction and up to 26% effectiveness improvement remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds Euclidean-versus-KL stability and positivity arguments, explicitly discusses quadratic utility-computation cost and amortization, and interprets the new experiments as supporting robustness to model initialization and independence from adaptation procedure. These materially expand the explanations and applicability arguments. The earlier appendix limitations concerning data quality, scalability, domains and bias are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public GitHub code-availability statement and explains computing the utility matrix once and reusing it. However, it removes v1's instruction-tuning split counts of 21,000/6,000/3,000 and the exact BGE and Prometheus checkpoint identifiers. The hyperparameter list remains largely unchanged, while the availability appendix still contains future-tense text and the anonymous repository address.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially recasts the research positioning around an information-theoretic framework and a claimed lack of principled grounding in LLM-feedback selection. Detailed discussions and references for CRAIG, TAGCOS and IFD are removed, along with several other cited works. This changes both the literature coverage and the distinction claimed against prior approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Method subsections are consolidated, experiments are reorganized around use cases with explicit takeaways, and a theoretical appendix is inserted before the existing appendices. Much of the conclusion and earlier appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Three new result tables substantially expand the main empirical presentation. Existing tables receive revised headers, formatting and captions; Figure 1 moves earlier, and Figure 2 is enlarged onto a dedicated page. The original illustrative figure, subset-size curves and judge-score histograms retain their underlying content despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added base-model, GSM-8k and full-fine-tuning experiments broaden validation, and the KL–PMI derivation adds a useful conditional connection. However, v3 removes reproducibility details, introduces a subset-size description inconsistent with its retained appendix, and incorrectly claims Euclidean distance guarantees positive utilities despite defining utility as a difference of distances (Appendix A.1). These empirical gains coexist with material documentation and reasoning regressions, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
